title: Cairn 0.4.1: the trusted base for M4, fuzzed
text: Cairn 0.4.1 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. Every Keychain call now goes through one serial queue for the process, so a forgetSecret racing a read of the same app's items no longer deadlocks inside Security's file-based keychain (#237), and a value that starts with a byte order mark reads back with it.

What VoiceOver and other assistive apps see of a scrolled list or a secure field was reviewed by hand; it is now two assume claims with a fuzz check each. ^1021: the accessibility tree holds exactly what a scroll area shows, walked through AppKit's own accessibility API on a real view. ^1022: a secure field shows nothing typed, and the debug socket's request log shows no secret. docs/trusted.md lists every assumption M4 added with its check; the full trusted fuzz run passes all 54 checks.
The registry's ledger check accepted 0.4.0 to 0.4.1, a patch release: two new claims and nothing retired. It serves the claims export, 54 active claims, for the claim pages.

title: Sky: refresh keeps the reader
caption: Three posts arrived and Refresh put them above: the post at the top of the view didn't move, and Sky offers ↑ 3 new posts to go back to the top. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Sky: scrolled to the end
caption: Scrolling to the end shows the list's end row; its appear loads the next page (30 → 43 posts). Reposts say who reposted; link cards are words for now. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Sky: the home feed
caption: Posts in Cairn's virtual list: avatars and images load from the fake PDS into fixed-size placeholders, text wraps, counts under each post. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Cairn 0.4.0: runtime scrolling, Action.appear, virtual lists and package-scoped fuzzing
text: Cairn 0.4.0 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. Scroll offsets belong to the runtime: a box names itself with Style.scrollRef, the runtime keeps its offset in UI.scroll, moves it for the wheel, trackpad and scroll keys, and clamps it after every step, and a scroll never reaches update (#225). A control with appear := true is told when it comes on screen, through Action.appear. The host's scroll sign is a new assume claim, ^1012.

VList.node lays out only the rows of a list that meet its box, so a runtime step costs about the same at 1,000 rows as at 100,000, with proofs that the rows built are exactly those in view and that the first row showing stays still when rows are inserted above it (#231). Fuzz targets are scoped by package: cairn fuzz runs only a package's own machines unless given --deps, and two targets with one name fail to compile (#224).

The registry's ledger check accepted 0.3.0 to 0.4.0: the only change to the ledger is ^1012. It is a minor release because Event, Action and Trigger gain constructors, so exhaustive matches need new cases; Style and UI gain defaulted fields, and settleFuel is 4. The registry checked the claims export, 54 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages.

title: Sky: a slow sign-in
caption: After a few seconds Sky says it's still signing in and offers Cancel. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Sky: offline
caption: Sign-in errors are words, not codes: here the service can't be reached. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Sky: a wrong app password
caption: A wrong password, said in words; the field is emptied as the request is sent. Offscreen render, fake PDS.

title: Sky: sign in
caption: Sky's sign-in screen (cairn#210): handle or email, the app password in a secure field (bullets only), the service. An offscreen render from the selftest against the fake PDS.

title: The runtime scrolls the fixture's rows
caption: Cairn's runtime now owns scroll offsets (#203). A scroll of 100,000 points over the fixture's 200 rows is clamped to the end, the app's state never sees it, and the end line, marked appear, hears that it came on screen: an Action.appear move counted in the app. Offscreen render through the real engine (Fixture --scroll-shots).

title: Cairn 0.3.0: the example apps leave, Keychain secrets, secure fields and scroll boxes
text: Cairn 0.3.0 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. The example apps (Counter, Basics, Todo, Clock, Tray, Gallery) live in their own package, cairn_examples, and their 71 claims keep their numbers there: cairn^202 is now cairn_examples^202, marked moved:cairn_examples in Cairn's ledger, which now holds only framework claims (#219).

A secret can live in the Keychain, and http can capture reply fields into it before Lean sees the body (#216). Text.SecureField shows bullets, never puts its text on the clipboard, in undo history or in any frame dump, and the host turns on secure event input while it has focus (#217). Style.scroll lays out scroll boxes, with proofs that what shows stays inside the box and a control is pressed only where it shows (#218). The frame format is version 11, and the 0.1.3 shims are gone.

The registry's ledger check accepted 0.2.5 to 0.3.0: moving and retiring released claims needs a new minor while at 0.x, and 0.2.6 would have been refused. It checked the claims export, 53 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages. Apps upgrade by naming an environment secret's source, matching http with eight arguments and importing Cairn.Abi for Cairn.Frame.Boundary.

title: Secure text field
caption: The fixture's Passcode field after typing seven characters: the frame holds seven bullets, never the text, and the host gives it the AXSecureTextField role with no value. An offscreen render of the frame (Renderer.image).

title: Yap on cairn_json
caption: Yap's overlay mid-dictation, now built on Cairn 0.2.5 with JSON from the cairn_json package instead of its own parser. Yap 0.1.0 is on the registry.

title: Cairn 0.2.5: closing the window quits cleanly
text: Cairn 0.2.5 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. Closing an app's window now quits it cleanly: the window delegate owns the window and shuts the view down before the app terminates. Before, AppKit also released the window on close, and a frame landing afterwards reached the freed window; Pairs 0.1.2 crashed that way. make selftest closes a real window with input, a timer and frames in flight (#199).

cairn builds fetch registry dependencies at the commit the manifest pins and turn Lake's lazy fetches off when every git dependency is on a registry: a stale checkout on Pairs went from 92 s to 4 s (#198). The tray's tick-rate selftest asserts the wall-clock rate on real hardware only (#195).

The registry checked its claims export, 122 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages. claims.lock is the same as 0.2.4's: no claim was retired, moved, changed or added, so it is a patch release.

title: Cairn 0.2.4, with a fuzzer that plays the host
text: Cairn 0.2.4 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. cairn fuzz now plays the host's side: it answers requests late and in any order, replies to cancelled ones, fires timers, moves the clock, sends subscription events and evicts images, within what the trusted claims allow, and checks that every image a frame draws is one the host holds (#189).

An app's Custom fuzz hooks take replies and subEvents generators, relations checked on every step, drained checks once the host has answered everything, and outstanding checks against the requests the runtime still holds (#189, #192).

The registry checked its claims export, 122 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages. claims.lock is the same as 0.2.3's: no claim was retired, moved, changed or added, so it is a patch release.

title: Cairn 0.2.3, with several apps a package and cairn bundle
text: Cairn 0.2.3 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. A package can hold several apps, and cairn build, size, bench and conformance take --app to link one (#177), as iamnbutler/cairn_examples does. cairn bundle wraps an app package's release build in a .app with the SwiftPM resource bundles it uses (#185).

The fuzzer now presses status-item buttons and menu items and takes App.minSize as the window's minimum, so Clock, Tray and Gallery are fuzzed (#178, #182). The click assumptions ^7 and ^214 moved from the examples into Cairn's trusted base, with pointer fuzz checks (#184).

The registry checked its claims export, 122 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages. claims.lock is the same as 0.2.2's: no claim was retired, moved, changed or added, so it is a patch release.

title: Pairs: the win screen
caption: All eight pairs of Patterns matched: the board gives way to the result, and the best moves and time for the pack are saved (they only ever improve, pairs^26).

title: Pairs: a pack that fails
caption: A pack with a missing image: Pairs says which face didn't load and leaves the game exactly as it was. A 404 manifest and a pack.json that isn't JSON are refused the same way.

title: Pairs: a pack loading over http
caption: A pack typed into the field loads beside the game from the URL tests' stub server, whose images answer after three seconds: the game goes on, with Cancel and a count of the images loaded. Choosing another pack or Cancel stops it; its late replies change nothing (pairs^28, ^29).

title: Pairs: the grid follows the window
caption: The same game in a wider, shorter window: Grid keeps four columns and shrinks the cards to fit the height; nothing scrolls. App.minSize from Grid.minBox keeps every card at least 64 points wide.

title: Pairs: a game in progress
caption: Pairs, the M3 memory game, built only from registry packages (cairn 0.2.2, cairn_json). Three pairs of Shapes are matched (green edges); the arrow and the heart don't match and turn back after a second. Rendered offscreen from the app's own frame.

title: Cairn 0.2.2, with a window minimum and an image budget
text: Cairn 0.2.2 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. An app declares its window's smallest size with App.minSize, and Grid.minBox gives the smallest box in which every card is at least its minimum width, proved for every size; the host keeps the window at least that big (#169, frame format 7). Sub.imageCache keeps the host's images within a byte budget, and the host tells the app with an evicted notice for every image it drops, so ready always means the pixels are there (#170, frame format 8).

The registry checked its claims export, 122 claims, against the ledger and serves it for the claim pages. No claim was retired, moved or changed, so it is a patch release; five are new, ^511–^513, ^1010 and ^1011.

title: Image cache under a budget
caption: Gallery runs an imageCache subscription with an 8 MiB budget. Load 24 fetches all 24 thumbnails; the host keeps the twelve on screen and drops the other page's, telling the app, which counts them as evicted and no longer takes them for loaded. Next page loads the dropped ones again, and the host drops the first page's in turn.

title: Cairn 0.2.1, with claim pages
text: Cairn 0.2.1 is out on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn. Requests in flight are capped at 6, with a queue and cancelRequest, frame format 6 (#151). Cairn.UI.Grid lays cards out in as many columns as the window fits, proved for every size (#160). cairn fuzz, claims, bench, size and conformance run on any app, and test/fixture is Cairn's own fixture app (#149).

cairn publish now sends the claims export as well as claims.lock. The registry checked its 117 claims against the ledger and serves it, so Cairn's claim pages group its moves and flows by place instead of showing only ledger rows (#156). No claim was retired, moved or changed, so it is a patch release; six are new, ^506–^510 and ^1009.

title: Try it: TodoMVC in the browser
caption: Every frame is one the app's Lean code drew, explored ahead of time; each control shows its claim id, its reading and a link to its claim page.

title: A floor on tile size
caption: Gallery asks the host to keep its window at least 1020 × 536: the smallest size, proved with Grid.minBox, at which every tile is 180 points wide. The demo drags the window narrower, shorter, then both, through the window's resize delegate as a person's drag goes; it stops at the minimum each time and the tiles stay 180 points wide.

title: Claim pages
caption: Every package on the registry gets claim pages, rendered by the site from the claims export cairn publish now sends: the overview grouped by place, then the Todos window, a flow's steps, a move, and one of the trusted base's assumptions. No agent and no screenshots of the apps: proofs, witnesses and where each claim is defined come straight from Lean. Shown here with Cairn's export from this branch; the live pages fill in once Cairn is published again. These replace the maps, and /map/ redirects here.

title: Gallery's grid follows the window
caption: Gallery's six tiles in a grid whose column count Lean computes from the window size: three columns at 1120 points, six at 1640, two at 860, in reading order throughout. The host only reports resize events; Lean proves the cells never overlap, stay inside the grid's box, take the most columns that fit, and that a click in a tile reaches that tile.

title: Many requests in flight, and Cancel
caption: Gallery asks for 24 thumbnails from a slow server. Lean's runtime sends six at a time and queues the rest; Cancel drops the queued ones and stops the six being fetched, and a late answer for a cancelled one changes nothing.

title: Cairn 0.2.0, with images
text: Cairn 0.2.0 is out, on the public registry as iamnbutler/cairn next to 0.1.3. It has images: Node.image, the loadImage effect, frame format 5 and the Gallery example (#132). import Cairn now links, the old everything-umbrella is CairnAll, and cairn new --bin makes a working app (#134). cairn-link links each dependency's libs from its cairn.toml, and Cairn's says libs = ["Cairn"] (#127).

It was going to be 0.1.4, and v0.1.4 is tagged, but the registry refused it: claim ^213's statement hash changed when Style gained its image field, and a published claim keeps its statement. Its meaning didn't change, so the same invariant is now ^225 and ^213 is retired. Retiring a released claim needs a new minor version while at 0.x, hence 0.2.0.

title: cairn new makes an app that links
text: Since the library split, the Cairn umbrella imported every proof and tool, none of which an app links, so an app that wrote import Cairn, as cairn new's template did, failed at the host's link on initialize_cairn_Cairn (#128). Now Cairn is the linked library's umbrella, with the claim commands at compile time only, and the everything-umbrella the ledger, the audit and the docs read is CairnAll. cairn new --bin writes a working app: a place, a move, its exports, the C declaration of its initializer and a host with a selftest. make check now builds one against the checkout, runs its selftest and locks its two claims, which takes about a minute.

title: Gallery: images
caption: Six image tiles, each a 200 × 150 Node.image that Lean lays out before any pixels exist: a PNG, a JPEG turned by its EXIF orientation, a GIF, a poster over https, a text file and a missing file. The host decodes with ImageIO and paints with Metal; Lean only learns the pixel size, or the fault, from the loadImage reply. Reload (^501) sends every tile back to its grey placeholder and reads each source again; Fit (^502) cycles cover, contain and stretch. Nothing moves when a picture arrives or fails. In the self test every tile was answered 6.8 ms after launch.

title: cairn_json, the first package outside the cairn repository
text: Yap's JSON parser and encoder is now its own registry package, cairn_json 0.1.0, in iamnbutler/cairn_json. It requires cairn ^0.1.2 from the registry, is pure Lean with no Swift and no extern, and leaves Yap's date arithmetic for a later cairn_date.

The library is 491 lines. 793 lines of proofs hold 49 theorems: decode (encode v) = some v and decode (pretty v) = some v for every value nested at most 512 deep, and that more fuel never changes what the parser answers. decode is total by construction, with no partial def. The axiom audit allows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and the kernel replays every declaration.

A trusted fuzz check compares it with Foundation's JSONSerialization: 220,164 documents per seed (valid, mutated, UTF-16 and UTF-32, random bytes and 164 edge cases), 5 seeds, 0 unexplained differences. The known ones are listed in its docs/trusted.md: numbers Foundation can't hold, a leading U+FEFF Foundation drops from strings, short UTF-16 and UTF-32 documents without a byte order mark, invalid UTF-8, and nesting 513 deep.
The commit is cairn_json's.

title: cairn-link links each dependency's libraries
text: bin/cairn-link no longer links Cairn's library by name (#118). It reads lake-manifest.json, finds the cairn.toml beside each dependency, transitive ones included, and links the Lean libraries that package lists under libs. Cairn's own cairn.toml now lists Cairn, so an app gets the same archive as before, and a library like cairn_json can be linked the same way.

It refuses a Lean module that ends up in two archives, which would be a duplicate symbol, and a dependency that is an app. A dependency with no cairn.toml is linked not at all; if linked code imports it, cairn-link names the package and says to give it one.

Checked with a throwaway app that depends on Cairn and on a second library package with its own libs: it links, and a small C program draws a frame through both. Yap builds against it with its existing --lib Yap and passes its selftest.

title: Cairn 0.1.3, on the public registry
text: Cairn 0.1.3 is out, and it is on the public registry at cairn.registry.nexthub.sh as iamnbutler/cairn, next to 0.1.2. Reading it needs no login: cairn add cairn finds the owner by name and writes the version range, and Lake fetches Cairn from the registry's git (#107, #109). /packages/ now reads the registry itself instead of sample data (#111).

The Cairn library is now only what an app links: 31 modules. Proofs, claims, fuzzing and tools are their own Lake libraries, so libcairn_Cairn.a went from 3.67 to 2.78 MB (#114). Three modules moved so the directories in lean/ have no cycles, and make lint now fails on one; the old names stay as shims until 0.2.0 (#110).
No claim changed, so it is a patch release. Yap moved to it with only its tag changed.

title: Cairn 0.1.2: libraries and apps
text: Cairn 0.1.2 is out. A package is now a library or an app, as in Cargo: cairn.toml has kind = "lib" or "bin", cairn new asks which, and /packages/ lists apps under their own tab (#103). Nothing can depend on an app.
cairn publish sends no docs. HTML from a publisher would run as the registry's site, so docs will be built from the source instead, as docs.rs does (#98).
The ledger now treats retiring a released claim as a breaking change: it needs a new major version, or a new minor one while at 0.x (#100). No claim changed in 0.1.2, so it is a patch release.

title: Cairn is a package, and Yap moved out
text: Cairn is now a package. An app lives in its own repository and depends on a tagged release, and one tag pins both halves: the Lean package and the Swift libraries. v0.1.0 is the first release (#80). v0.1.1 fixes cairn doc, which failed in apps because it read its stylesheet from the app (#91).
Yap moved out first. It lives in its own repository, yap-cairn, and depends on Cairn v0.1.0 like any other app would. Its Lean, proofs, fuzzers, Swift host and benches left this repository with it.

Claim ids are now scoped by package. Cairn's are cairn^N and Yap's are yap^N, so “a shortcut never sends” is yap^311. Cairn's claims.lock still lists Yap's old ids, marked moved:yap, so they can never be issued here again.

title: The cairn command and packages
text: There is now a cairn command (#79). cairn new starts a package in its own repository with its claim scope set, cairn add depends on another package, and cairn build runs Lake, links the Lean into one library and builds the Swift host. cairn doc writes the package's docs, and cairn publish and cairn login talk to a registry. It has unit tests, and it has been run against a stand-in registry but not a deployed one yet.

The registry is nextpm, a package registry, with a new cairn kind (nextpm #22). It has an index Lake reads natively, the source served over git, and a build cache, so that lake cache get downloads prebuilt Lean. Its claim ledger refuses a version that drops, renumbers or redefines an id. /packages/ shows a registry's packages, and until one is running it shows sample data (#78).
Publishers no longer upload docs. A registry now refuses HTML from a publisher (nextpm #23), and docs will be built from the source by a builder we run, the way docs.rs works (#94).

title: Developer docs and the API reference
text: Developer docs are up at /docs, laid out like Rust's bookshelf: the Cairn Book, Cairn by Example, reference pages, and guides to working on Cairn itself (#76). Every code sample is included from a source file that make check compiles, so a sample can't drift from the code it shows. Moving an included region fails the build until the page is fixed.

The API reference at /docs/api/ is generated by cairn doc, Cairn's answer to rustdoc (#77). It reads the Lean environment directly instead of using doc-gen4. On TodoMVC, doc-gen4 took 185 s and wrote 227 MB, almost all of it Lean's own library. Each claim appears on its module's page with its statement, evidence and proofs. A Lean block in a doc comment is a doc test that make check runs.
Every heading on the site also has an id now, and a # that copies a link to it (#72).

title: Yap against the original under Instruments
text: Yap on Cairn was measured against the original Yap with Apple's Instruments rather than Cairn's own tools (#65). At 60 Hz the two overlays now pace the same, at 59.3 and 59.9 frames a second, with no hitches in either.

While recording, Cairn used 205 ms of CPU a second, against the original's 82. Most of that went to redrawing the menu bar's status item on every frame. Once its properties were written only when they change, an A/B run went from 197 to 98 ms/s.

The overlay now appears only once the microphone is running, as in the original, so a microphone that fails no longer flashes it (#68, yap^349). On a 120 Hz display, Cairn drew 118 frames a second where the original draws 60. It's now capped at 60, and it checks files every 2 s, as the original does (#69). The idle runs and a check on a 60 Hz display are still to do (#70).

title: Yap on Cairn: the overlay
caption: Yap's dictation overlay on Cairn, driven by a synthetic voice: recording with a moving tape waveform and a two-line live preview, then transcribing, then typed. The state, view and layout are Lean; the waveform is a host-drawn paint node running the original's Metal shader.

title: Clock: effects
caption: Cairn's first effects. A stopwatch whose time, ticks, sounds and lap file come from the host as replies to requests Lean makes: Lap plays a sound, Save writes the laps to a file, Reset clears them and Load reads them back. Timers fire within 1–2 ms; a click → read file → frame round trip is 1.5 ms (p50).

title: TodoMVC in Lean
caption: The full TodoMVC, written in Lean and running natively on the Mac. Add, complete, double-click to edit, filter, clear completed, and toggle all. Every control is a claim (^202 to ^211). On the real app, 999 of 1,000 generated conformance sequences matched the Lean model. The one miss is a known edge case: a click that ends an edit can be dropped, as in a browser.

title: Basics: the first Lean app
caption: A whole app written in Lean: adding, ticking and deleting items. Lean decides the layout, focus, text editing and hit testing; Swift only draws. Every control is a claim (^101 to ^104). Lean proves that an item's Delete button exists exactly when the item does, and that the 'items left' count is right.

title: The host, with text
caption: The new AppKit host painting through the Metal renderer: Core Text glyphs from an atlas, a caret, a focused field, a checkbox and a list. Typing goes through the Mac's text-input path, and every control in the accessibility tree is named by its claim id (^1 field, ^2 checkbox, ^3 Add, ^4#1 the new item). This app is the host's test fixture, with its frames built in Swift; the next video is the same host running a Lean app.

title: Boundary spike
caption: The first thing on screen. Lean owns the state, the layout and the hit test; Swift forwards clicks and paints Lean's rectangles with Metal. The bar is the count (no text rendering yet). Reset (red) exists only while the count is above zero, which is proved in Lean, and here it's pressed through the accessibility tree.
